To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the use of video for background awareness in an office setting is a complex social activity that is not well suited for a simple, one-way video display.

the design of video applications should: (a) allow users to choose when to use the video application, (b) allow users to control what others can see, and (c) provide users with a means of communicating their intentions to others.

the user interface of the video application should be redesigned to: (1) reduce self-presentation concerns, (2) reduce privacy concerns, (3) reduce surveillance concerns, (4) increase the ability of users to control their video snapshots, and (5) increase the ability for users to obtain audience cues.
